style: Fiery Rasta chanters, fire-and-brimstone, wailing held vowels, long chanted lines, preaching and raging. Heavy half-time reggae riddim at 80: a deep punchy kick, a dry cracking rimshot snare, an organ bubble and a muted guitar skank on the offbeat, a massive overdriven sound-system sub carrying the tune, dub sirens, tape delay and spring reverb thrown off the line-ends and the snare, a church organ. Dark, heavy and menacing. Polished punchy modern mix, crisp top end, wide stereo, a catchy hook the room says with him. Two of them trade the verses, loud and in front, aggressive and cutting, laid back behind the beat on the slow half-time pulse, heavy and unhurried, every word clear. Every vocal sound is a word from the lyrics.
